newsitem.title: USA: Lear acquisitions fuel Q3 revenue growth.
newsitem.headline: Lear acquisitions fuel Q3 revenue growth.

text.p: Lear Corp said its third quarter revenues rose more than 39 percent because of internal growth and the acquisition of Automotive Industries Inc and Masland Corp in the past year.
Lear said its revenues increased to $1.506 billion from $1.081 billion in the third quarter of 1995.
Masland contributed $138.5 million of the $425 million increase in revenues, while Automotive industries contributed $97.4 million.
Lear reported that its net income for the third quarter nearly tripled, to $24.8 million.
Geographically, it said about 29 percent of the third quarter's $425.0 million sales increase was attributable to international operations.

Sales in the U.S. and Canada rose about $283 million to $1.0 billion, while European sales increased 19 percent to $331.4 million. Sales in Mexico and other world regions more than doubled, rising to $160.8 million from $71.7 million.

"We are pleased with the $16.3 million increase in quarterly earnings as well as the successful completion of our $700 million securities offerings during the quarter," Lear Chairman Kenneth Way said in a statement. "Lear's record-breaking performance again demonstrates our ability to benefit from market share growth, globalization of the automotive industry, increasing interior content and productivity gains."
